```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4,
                      fig.path = "output/figures/")
```

**How to run this file.** This one file is the whole analysis. Knit it from
start to finish; no other script has to be run first. It reads four files
from the `data/` folder next to it:

- `openesm_0075.rds`, the Open Play daily diary from openESM. If it is
  missing, the `download` chunk downloads and saves it (this needs the
  internet).
- `survey_intake.csv.gz`, the Open Play intake survey from the project's
  repository (<https://github.com/digital-wellbeing/open-play>), which
  supplies the demographics.
- `game_classification.csv` and `game_classification_excluded.csv`, the
  hand-reviewed lookup files that give each game title's genre.

The file cleans the diary, builds the daily table, runs the clustering and
the principal components, fits every supervised model on feature sets A and
B, and saves the results to `output/final_results.rds` for the report.
Fitting the models takes most of the knit time.

**The test set stays locked until the final model is chosen.** The chunks
that touch the test set only run when `run_test_set` is `TRUE`. Keep it
`FALSE` while reading the cross-validated comparison (Section 8), then set it
to `TRUE` for one final knit.

```{r test-switch}
run_test_set <- TRUE
```

**Saved model fits.** Each `train()` result is saved to
`output/model_fits/` as soon as it is fit. If the folder is missing, every
model is fit from scratch. Later knits read the saved fit instead of
refitting, so editing the text or the tables does not cost another long run:
with the saved fits a knit takes a few minutes, and refitting every model
took about 1.5 hours on a laptop with the folds in parallel. Set
`refit_models` to `TRUE` (or delete the folder) whenever anything before
Section 8 changes, and once more for the knit that is submitted (the handout:
"knit clean before submitting"). The fits are exactly reproducible with the
same package versions (Section 12), so that knit should give the same
numbers.

```{r refit-switch}
refit_models <- FALSE
```

```{r packages}
library(openesm)     # get_dataset() and cite()
library(dplyr)      # data manipulation and the pipe
library(tidyr)       # pivot_longer()
library(ggplot2)     # plots
library(naniar)      # vis_miss() and gg_miss_var()
library(rsample)     # group_initial_split()
library(recipes)     # imputation, dummy coding, and scaling inside the pipeline
library(cluster)     # silhouette()
library(caret)       # train(), groupKFold(), resamples(), varImp()
library(glmnet)      # elastic net
library(ranger)      # random forests
library(doParallel)  # fits the cross-validation folds in parallel

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

# Every file is read from data/ and written to output/, both in the folder
# that holds this Rmd. Knitting runs from that folder, and so does running
# chunks by hand after opening the .Rproj.
data_path <- function(file) file.path("data", file)
out_path  <- function(file) file.path("output", file)
dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# 1. Research Questions

**Supervised.** Using same-day predictors and stable person characteristics
from the intake survey, how well can we predict a player's **life
satisfaction** on a day they played video games? Life satisfaction is the
daily item "I was satisfied with my life today," rated on a 0 to 100 slider,
so the target is **continuous**. The predictors are:

- the six Basic Needs in Games (BANGS) items about the most recent session;
- the type of game played and who the person played with that day;
- sleep quality, the type of day, and the platform;
- whether a stressful event occurred, which kinds, and how stressful the
  worst one was;
- six daily basic-needs items (satisfaction and frustration of autonomy,
  competence, and relatedness);
- demographics and life circumstances from the intake survey: age, gender,
  employment, education, relationship status, and caring for children.

Every daily predictor comes from the **same day's** survey as the target, so
the model describes what goes together on a day. It does not forecast.
Affective valence ("How are you feeling right now?") is **not** a predictor.
It is answered in the same sitting and correlates highly with life
satisfaction (Section 3).

The users are designers of digital well-being tools, such as a check-in at
the end of a play session that flags players who may be having a bad day.

**Unsupervised.**

- **Dimensions of a day (PCA).** We reduce the six daily basic-needs items. We
  expect two components, general satisfaction and general frustration, rather
  than one per need.
- **Types of play days (K-means).** We cluster the play days on the six
  BANGS items, which describe the day's most recent gaming session. The
  proposal expected days built around a "toxic competitive session," a
  "low improvement session," and a "satisfying solo session."

# 2. Get the Data

## The download

The diary is the `get_dataset("0075")` output, downloaded once and saved to
`data/openesm_0075.rds`.

```{r download, eval = !file.exists(data_path("openesm_0075.rds"))}
# only runs if the saved file is missing
open_play <- get_dataset("0075")
saveRDS(open_play, data_path("openesm_0075.rds"))
```

```{r read}
open_play <- readRDS(data_path("openesm_0075.rds"))
raw <- open_play$data          # the diary as downloaded

intake <- read.csv(data_path("survey_intake.csv.gz"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# the expected file: one row per person per day
dim(raw)
stopifnot(nrow(raw) == 16346, n_distinct(raw$id) == 1284,
          !anyDuplicated(raw[c("id", "day")]))
c(people = n_distinct(raw$id))
```

The citation for the references section:

```{r cite}
cite(open_play)
```

## The codebook

The codebook comes with the data, one row per variable. The item wording is
in `details` and the response codes are in `labels`.

```{r codebook}
codebook <- open_play$metadata$features[[1]]

codebook %>%
  filter(name %in% c("gaming_toxic", "needs_autonomy_satisfied",
                     "life_satisfaction", "sleep_quality",
                     "how_stressful_health")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(details, labels), ~ gsub("\n", " ", .x))) %>%
  select(name, details, labels) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

# 3. Build the Daily Table

## What is in a row

Open Play surveys once a day at 2 PM, so each row is already one person on
one day (`beep` is always 1). No aggregation is needed and there is no
minimum-prompts rule. The work is recoding and restricting to play days.

```{r rows}
table(beep = raw$beep)
```

## Clean the diary

16,346 days are kept. The cleaning script does the following:

- **Checkboxes to No/Yes factors, with skip-pattern blanks recoded rather
  than imputed.** The social-play boxes are "No" on days without play. The
  stress event types are "No" on days without a stressful event.
- **Summaries.** The four social-play boxes were summarized into
  `play_context`, and the typed platform answers were grouped into
  `platform`, each with a "Did not play" level. The rules are listed later
  in this section.
- **Stress severity** (four options) is an ordered factor, and `stress_worst`
  is the highest severity that day.
- **Swapped columns fixed.** In the source data, the severity ratings for the
  "health" and "other" events are stored in each other's columns. The
  cleaning swaps them back.
- **Type of day.** Holiday and vacation day are combined into one level.
- **Dropped:**
  - bookkeeping (`date`, `beep`, `survey_duration`, `baseline_day`,
    `ideal_baseline_day`, `n_valid`, `original_wave`);
  - the attention-check and duplicate-item columns for the needs scale;
  - free text (`most_recent_game`, `displaced_activity`).

```{r clean-daily}
# 1. The swapped stress ratings. In the source data the "health" and "other"
# severity ratings sit in each other's columns: every day with the health box
# checked has its rating in how_stressful_other and none in
# how_stressful_health, and the reverse holds for "other". Check this, then
# swap them back. The swap is made on a copy, so raw stays as downloaded.
swap_check <- c(
  health_checked_other_rated = sum(!is.na(raw$stress_events_health) & !is.na(raw$how_stressful_other)),
  health_checked             = sum(!is.na(raw$stress_events_health)),
  other_checked_health_rated = sum(!is.na(raw$stress_events_other) & !is.na(raw$how_stressful_health)),
  other_checked              = sum(!is.na(raw$stress_events_other)))
swap_check
stopifnot(swap_check[1] == swap_check[2], swap_check[3] == swap_check[4])

src <- raw %>%
  rename(how_stressful_health = how_stressful_other,
         how_stressful_other  = how_stressful_health)

# 2. Recode
yes_no <- function(x) factor(x, levels = c("No", "Yes"))

# A checkbox holds its label when checked and NA when not. On days the
# question was not shown (no play, no stress), unchecked means "No".
# `asked` is TRUE when shown, FALSE when skipped by design, and NA when the
# gate question itself is missing.
checkbox <- function(x, asked) {
  factor(ifelse(is.na(asked), NA, ifelse(!is.na(x), "Yes", "No")),
         levels = c("No", "Yes"))
}

social_cols <- c("social_singleplayer", "social_friends_realworld",
                 "social_friends_online", "social_strangers")
event_cols  <- grep("^stress_events_", names(src), value = TRUE)
sev_cols    <- grep("^how_stressful_", names(src), value = TRUE)
sev_levels  <- c("No event", "Not at all", "Not very", "Somewhat", "Very")

daily <- src %>%
  mutate(
    played24hr = yes_no(played24hr),
    had_stress = yes_no(had_stress),

    # who they played with: days without play are "No" for every box; a play
    # day with no box checked is NA (everyone who played, played with someone
    # or alone)
    no_social_box = rowSums(!is.na(across(all_of(social_cols)))) == 0,
    across(all_of(social_cols), ~ checkbox(.x, asked = played24hr == "Yes")),
    across(all_of(social_cols), ~ replace(.x, played24hr == "Yes" & no_social_box, NA)),

    # one summary of the social context, with its own level for non-play days
    play_context = case_when(
      played24hr == "No" ~ "Did not play",
      social_strangers == "Yes" &
        (social_friends_realworld == "Yes" | social_friends_online == "Yes") ~ "Friends + strangers",
      social_strangers == "Yes" ~ "Strangers only",
      social_friends_realworld == "Yes" | social_friends_online == "Yes" ~ "Friends only",
      social_singleplayer == "Yes" ~ "Solo only"),
    play_context = factor(play_context,
                          levels = c("Did not play", "Solo only", "Friends only",
                                     "Friends + strangers", "Strangers only")),

    # platform of the most recent session, grouped; typed "Other" answers
    # (PC, laptop, Chromebook, ...) stay "Other"
    platform = case_when(
      played24hr == "No" ~ "Did not play",
      most_recent_game_plat == "Steam"       ~ "Steam",
      most_recent_game_plat == "Xbox"        ~ "Xbox",
      most_recent_game_plat == "Playstation" ~ "PlayStation",
      grepl("^Nintendo", most_recent_game_plat) ~ "Nintendo",
      most_recent_game_plat %in% c("iOS", "Android", "AMAZON TABLET") ~ "Mobile",
      !is.na(most_recent_game_plat) ~ "Other"),
    platform = factor(platform, levels = c("Did not play", "Steam", "Xbox",
                                           "PlayStation", "Nintendo",
                                           "Mobile", "Other")),

    # stress event types: "No" on days with had_stress = "No"; NA on a "Yes"
    # day with no type checked (the types are unknown)
    any_event_box = rowSums(!is.na(across(all_of(event_cols)))) > 0,
    across(all_of(event_cols), ~ checkbox(.x, asked = had_stress == "Yes")),
    across(all_of(event_cols), ~ replace(.x, had_stress == "Yes" & !any_event_box, NA)),
    n_stress_events = rowSums(across(all_of(event_cols), ~ .x == "Yes")),

    # severity (1 to 4 in the source) as an ordered factor with a "No event"
    # level below "Not at all": four response options, so not numeric
    worst_raw = suppressWarnings(
      do.call(pmax, c(across(all_of(sev_cols)), na.rm = TRUE))),
    across(all_of(sev_cols),
           ~ factor(ifelse(is.na(had_stress), NA, ifelse(is.na(.x), 0, .x)),
                    levels = 0:4, labels = sev_levels, ordered = TRUE)),
    across(all_of(sev_cols), ~ replace(.x, had_stress == "Yes" & !any_event_box, NA)),
    stress_worst = factor(case_when(
      had_stress == "No"  ~ 0,
      had_stress == "Yes" ~ worst_raw),    # NA if "Yes" but nothing rated
      levels = 0:4, labels = sev_levels, ordered = TRUE),

    # type of day: holiday and vacation day (2 to 3% of days each) both mean a
    # weekday off, so they are combined
    day_type = factor(day_type,
                      levels = c("Regular work day", "Regular day off", "Weekend",
                                 "Holiday", "Vacation day", "Other (please specify):"),
                      labels = c("Work day", "Day off", "Weekend",
                                 "Holiday or vacation", "Holiday or vacation", "Other"))
    # numeric items stay numbers: gaming_* and needs_* (1 to 7), sleep_quality
    # (1 to 5), affective_valence and life_satisfaction (0 to 100)
  )

# an event type that was checked must have a severity rating, and only then
for (e in sub("stress_events_", "", event_cols)) {
  sev <- if (e == "home") "how_stressful_home_issue" else paste0("how_stressful_", e)
  stopifnot(all((daily[[paste0("stress_events_", e)]] == "Yes") ==
                  (daily[[sev]] > "No event"), na.rm = TRUE))
}

# 3. Keep the variables, one row per person per day, in id and day order
daily <- daily %>%
  arrange(id, day) %>%
  select(id, day, affective_valence, life_satisfaction, sleep_quality, day_type,
         played24hr, starts_with("gaming_"), all_of(social_cols), play_context, platform,
         starts_with("needs_"),
         had_stress, all_of(event_cols), n_stress_events, all_of(sev_cols), stress_worst)

# the clean table has the same person days as the download
stopifnot(nrow(daily) == nrow(raw),
          setequal(paste(daily$id, daily$day), paste(raw$id, raw$day)))
dim(daily)
```

The attention check failed on no day, so dropping it loses nothing:

```{r attention-check}
table(bpnsfs_failed_att_check = raw$bpnsfs_failed_att_check, useNA = "ifany")
```

## What the analysis adds

**Added back from the download** (joined by `id` and `day`):

- `most_recent_game`, used once to build the game type (below). It is not a
  predictor.
- `date`, used only for two checks: platform missingness by month (Section 4)
  and the intake-timing leakage check (Section 7).

**Left out of the analysis:**

- **Affective valence** ("How are you feeling right now?"). It is answered in
  the same sitting as life satisfaction and is close to the same thing on a
  given day (correlation below). A model that used it would mostly translate
  valence into life satisfaction. It is the target in another form.
- **`n_stress_events` and the seven individual severity ratings.** The
  stress information enters as `had_stress`, the seven event types, and the
  worst rating that day.
- **The four social-play checkboxes.** They enter through `play_context`.
- **Lags.** Every predictor here is from the same day, so no lags are built.

```{r valence}
round(cor(daily$affective_valence, daily$life_satisfaction, use = "complete.obs"), 2)
```

```{r add-back}
dat <- daily %>%
  select(-affective_valence, -n_stress_events, -starts_with("how_stressful_")) %>%
  left_join(raw %>% select(id, day, date, most_recent_game), by = c("id", "day"))

stopifnot(nrow(dat) == nrow(daily))
dim(dat)
```

## Play days only

The six BANGS items are asked only on days the person played in the last 24
hours. Our question is about play days, so the daily table keeps only those
days, as the proposal says. Days with a missing answer to the play question
are dropped with them.

```{r play-days}
table(played24hr = dat$played24hr, useNA = "always")

# BANGS items exist only on play days
table(played = dat$played24hr, has_bangs = !is.na(dat$gaming_toxic), useNA = "ifany")

counts <- data.frame(step = "All diary days",
                     days = nrow(dat), people = n_distinct(dat$id))

# days with no answer to the play question, and how many also lack the target
played_missing <- c(days      = sum(is.na(dat$played24hr)),
                    no_target = sum(is.na(dat$played24hr) & is.na(dat$life_satisfaction)))
played_missing

dat <- dat %>%
  filter(played24hr %in% "Yes") %>%
  select(-played24hr) %>%
  mutate(play_context = droplevels(play_context),   # "Did not play" no longer occurs
         platform     = droplevels(platform))

counts <- rbind(counts, data.frame(step = "Play days",
                                   days = nrow(dat), people = n_distinct(dat$id)))

# no play day was left with the non-play levels
stopifnot(!any(c(levels(dat$play_context), levels(dat$platform)) == "Did not play"))
```

The `r played_missing[["days"]]` days with no answer to the play question are
nearly all empty surveys. `r played_missing[["no_target"]]` of them have no
life satisfaction rating either, so they could not have been used anyway.

**Play days with no gaming answers.** On some play days the person said they
played, then skipped every gaming question: no title, no social box, no
platform, and no BANGS item. These days are dropped:

- The question is about what a day of gaming was like, and these days say
  nothing about it. Every gaming predictor would be imputed, so each day
  would add filled-in values, not information.
- They would also be miscoded. A blank title is "Unclassified," and the
  game-type rules (below) read a missing play context as solo.

```{r no-gaming}
bangs <- c("gaming_autonomy", "gaming_wish_else", "gaming_progress",
           "gaming_disappointed", "gaming_relationships", "gaming_toxic")
needs <- c("needs_autonomy_satisfied", "needs_autonomy_frustrated",
           "needs_competence_satisfied", "needs_competence_frustrated",
           "needs_relatedness_satisfied", "needs_relatedness_frustrated")

no_title  <- is.na(dat$most_recent_game) | trimws(dat$most_recent_game) == ""
no_gaming <- no_title & is.na(dat$play_context) & is.na(dat$platform) &
             rowSums(!is.na(dat[bangs])) == 0

no_gaming_n <- c(days = sum(no_gaming),
                 with_target = sum(no_gaming & !is.na(dat$life_satisfaction)))
no_gaming_n

dat <- dat[!no_gaming, ]

counts <- rbind(counts, data.frame(step = "Play days with gaming answers",
                                   days = nrow(dat), people = n_distinct(dat$id)))
counts
```

`r no_gaming_n[["days"]]` play days had no gaming answers. Only
`r no_gaming_n[["with_target"]]` of them had a life satisfaction rating, so
dropping them loses `r no_gaming_n[["with_target"]]` usable days.

## Checking the recoding

**Placeholder codes.** The numeric items are all inside their allowed ranges,
so there are no codes like 99 or -99:

```{r ranges}
sapply(dat[c("life_satisfaction", bangs, needs, "sleep_quality")], range, na.rm = TRUE)
sapply(dat[c("life_satisfaction", bangs, needs, "sleep_quality")], class)
```

**Ordinal items** follow one rule. An item with five or more ordered
response options is treated as numeric, and one with fewer is treated as an
ordered factor.

- The BANGS and needs items (1 to 7) and sleep quality (1 to 5) are numeric.
- The worst-stressor rating has four options, so it is an ordered factor
  (below).

**Type of day**, with holiday and vacation already combined:

```{r day-type}
table(dat$day_type, useNA = "always")
```

**Who they played with and the platform.** These were summarized in the
cleaning (Section 3) with these rules:

- play context is friends + strangers, strangers only, friends only, or solo
  only;
- iOS and Android are combined as Mobile, and typed "Other" platforms stay
  Other.

A play day with no social box checked would have a missing play context.
Every such day also had no other gaming answers and was dropped above, so
none remain.

```{r play-context}
table(dat$play_context, useNA = "always")
table(dat$platform, useNA = "always")
```

## Type of game

`most_recent_game` is typed free text. We clean each
title (lowercase, accents removed, punctuation stripped) and look up its
genre in two files:

- `game_classification.csv`, a hand-reviewed list of titles and genres;
- `game_classification_excluded.csv`, the titles that were only named on
  solo days or are single-player games. These were classified by matching
  patterns in the titles and not reviewed by hand.

Each genre is then coded by **who the other people in the game are**:

- single-player;
- non-competitive (co-op, MMO, sandbox, casual);
- individual competition;
- team competition;
- unknown.

**On days with other players** (friends, strangers, or both), these rules
apply:

- Games that can be played either solo or in a squad (Fortnite, PUBG,
  Warzone), Minecraft, and Roblox are coded from who the person played with:
  with friends, team competition; strangers only, individual competition.
- Single-player games with a co-op mode count as non-competitive.
- Titles neither lookup file can classify are "Unknown."

**On solo-only days, the person's own answer decides.** On a solo-only day the person
answered "Single-player games only" when asked what kind of social
interaction they took part in while gaming. Every game on such a day is
coded **single-player**, whatever its genre in the lookup files. The reasons:

- **The lookup only says what a game can be.** Many games coded as
  competitive or co-op also have modes played alone or against the computer
  (Call of Duty, Mario Kart, WWE 2K25, Minecraft, Genshin Impact). The person
  knows which mode they played. The lookup does not.
- **The session items are answered from the person's own view of the
  session.** The BANGS items (relationships, toxicity, disappointment) ask how
  the most recent session felt. They have to be read in the context the
  person reported, not in one we assign from the title.
- **We do not overrule what people said in the survey.** Where the person's
  description of their gaming day and our classification of the game
  disagree, the person's description wins.
- **It also covers titles the lookup cannot classify.** The solo-day titles
  come from the lookup file that was not reviewed by hand, which leaves many
  single-player games "Unclassified" (Pokémon Shield, Final Fantasy VII
  Rebirth, Civilization). And it removes cases where similar games got
  different codes (College Football 25 as individual competition, College
  Football 26 as unclassified).

The table after the chunk shows what the genre rules would have given on the
solo-only days.

```{r game-lookup}
clean_name <- function(x) {
  x <- iconv(x, from = "UTF-8", to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT", sub = "")
  x <- gsub("[^a-z0-9 ]", " ", tolower(x))
  x <- trimws(gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ", x))
  x[is.na(x)] <- ""
  x
}

# the reviewed list comes first, so its genre wins if a title is in both files
lookup_cols  <- c("game", "genre", "classified_by")
genre_lookup <- rbind(
  read.csv(data_path("game_classification.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[, lookup_cols],
  read.csv(data_path("game_classification_excluded.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)[, lookup_cols])
genre_lookup <- genre_lookup[!duplicated(genre_lookup$game), ]

# a title missing from both files stops the knit rather than being guessed
genre_of <- function(name) {
  genre <- genre_lookup$genre[match(name, genre_lookup$game)]
  if (anyNA(genre)) stop("Not in the lookup files: ",
                         paste(unique(name[is.na(genre)]), collapse = ", "))
  genre
}

# answers that name more than one game; each game is classified on its own
multi_game <- list(
  "baldurs gate 3 echoes of the plum grove" = c("baldurs gate 3", "echoes of the plum grove"),
  "btd 6 roblox"                       = c("btd 6", "roblox"),
  "btd 6 rematch"                      = c("btd 6", "rematch"),
  "btd 6 warframe roblox"              = c("btd 6", "warframe", "roblox"),
  "btd 6 warframe roblox terraria"     = c("btd 6", "warframe", "roblox", "terraria"),
  "dbd roblox"                         = c("dbd", "roblox"),
  "dead by daylight and roblox"        = c("dead by daylight", "roblox"),
  "dune awakening erenshor"            = c("dune awakening", "erenshor"),
  "expedition 33 and fortnite"         = c("expedition 33", "fortnite"),
  "fallout 4 dead by daylight"         = c("fallout 4", "dead by daylight"),
  "fornite and rocket league"          = c("fortnite", "rocket league"),
  "fortnite and avowed"                = c("fortnite", "avowed"),
  "fortnite and battle teams 2"        = c("fortnite", "battle teams 2"),
  "fortnite call of duty"              = c("fortnite", "call of duty"),
  "gta v and schedule 1"               = c("gta v", "schedule 1"),
  "marvel rivals and roblox"           = c("marvel rivals", "roblox"),
  "marvel rivals smurfvillage"         = c("marvel rivals", "smurfs village"),
  "marvel snap supervive"              = c("marvel snap", "supervive"),
  "minecraft and marvel rivals"        = c("minecraft", "marvel rivals"),
  "minecraft bf4 nhl 25"               = c("minecraft", "battlefield 4", "nhl"),
  "minecraft roblox"                   = c("minecraft", "roblox"),
  "mix of shcedule 1 and game of thrones" = c("schedule 1", "game of thrones"),
  "nba 2k25 wwe 2k25"                  = c("nba 2k25", "wwe 2k25"),
  "nhl 25 minecraft and battlefield 4" = c("nhl", "minecraft", "battlefield 4"),
  "no man s sky deep rock galactic"    = c("no man s sky", "deep rock galactic"),
  "pokemon go and royal match"         = c("pokemon go", "royal match"),
  "powerwashing simulator club penguin" = c("powerwash simulator", "club penguin"),
  "roblox btd 6"                       = c("roblox", "btd 6"),
  "roblox btd 6 limbus company"        = c("roblox", "btd 6", "limbus company"),
  "roblox btd 6 osrs"                  = c("roblox", "btd 6", "osrs"),
  "roblox fortnite"                    = c("roblox", "fortnite"),
  "sun haven coral island"             = c("sun haven", "coral island"),
  "sun haven echoes of the plum grove" = c("sun haven", "echoes of the plum grove"),
  "the walking dead fortnite"          = c("the walking dead", "fortnite"),
  "word find stud io poker"            = c("word find", "poker"))
```

```{r game-type}
code_competition <- function(game_category, play_context) {
  with_friends <- play_context %in% c("Friends only", "Friends + strangers")
  with_others  <- with_friends | play_context %in% "Strangers only"
  case_when(
    game_category == "Solo or co-op" & with_others ~ "Non-competitive",
    game_category == "Solo or co-op" ~ "Single-player",
    game_category == "Competitive team" ~ "Team competition",
    game_category == "Squad or solo" & with_friends ~ "Team competition",
    game_category == "Squad or solo" ~ "Individual competition",
    game_category == "Head-to-head" ~ "Individual competition",
    game_category %in% c("Online co-op / MMO", "Sandbox / social",
                         "Casual / mobile") ~ "Non-competitive",
    game_category %in% c("Minecraft", "Roblox") & with_friends ~ "Team competition",
    game_category %in% c("Minecraft", "Roblox") & with_others ~ "Individual competition",
    game_category %in% c("Minecraft", "Roblox") ~ "Non-competitive",
    game_category == "Mobile (single-player)" ~ "Single-player",
    game_category == "Single-player" ~ "Single-player",
    TRUE ~ "Unknown")
}

# several games named: on days with others, single-player games are dropped;
# if the games left agree the day gets their code, otherwise "Unknown"
combine_games <- function(name, play_context) {
  codes <- unique(code_competition(genre_of(multi_game[[name]]), play_context))
  with_others <- play_context %in% c("Friends only", "Friends + strangers",
                                     "Strangers only")
  if (with_others && any(codes != "Single-player")) {
    codes <- setdiff(codes, "Single-player")
  }
  if (length(codes) == 1) codes else "Unknown"
}

# code_competition() reads a missing play context as solo, so a missing context
# is allowed only on days with no title (no gaming answers at all)
stopifnot(all(clean_name(dat$most_recent_game)[is.na(dat$play_context)] == ""))

dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(game_clean    = clean_name(most_recent_game),
         game_category = genre_of(game_clean),
         game_type     = code_competition(game_category, play_context))

several <- dat$game_category == "Multiple games"
dat$game_type[several] <- mapply(combine_games, dat$game_clean[several],
                                 as.character(dat$play_context[several]))

# the solo-day rule: on a "single-player games only" day, every game is
# single-player. First, what the genre rules alone gave on those days:
solo_day <- dat$play_context %in% "Solo only"
solo_rule <- table(genre_rules_gave = dat$game_type[solo_day])
solo_rule
dat$game_type[solo_day] <- "Single-player"

dat$game_type <- factor(dat$game_type,
                        levels = c("Single-player", "Non-competitive",
                                   "Individual competition", "Team competition",
                                   "Unknown"))

table(dat$game_type, useNA = "always")

# how the game type lines up with who the person played with
table(play_context = dat$play_context, game_type = dat$game_type, useNA = "ifany")
```

Of the `r format(sum(solo_rule), big.mark = ",")` solo-only days, the genre
rules alone would have given
`r sum(solo_rule) - solo_rule[["Single-player"]] - solo_rule[["Unknown"]]` a
competitive or non-competitive code and left
`r format(solo_rule[["Unknown"]], big.mark = ",")` unknown. The person's
answer codes them all as single-player. Game type and play context now overlap on
these days by design, so the importance of the two (Section 9) should be read
together.

On days with other players, the most recent game can still be a
single-player game
(`r sum(dat$game_type == "Single-player" & !dat$play_context %in% "Solo only")`
days). That is not a contradiction. The play context covers the whole day,
while the game type describes the most recent session.

## Stress

The stress predictors are:

- `had_stress` ("Did anything happen to you in the last 24 hours that most
  people would consider stressful?");
- the seven event types as No/Yes factors;
- `stress_worst`, the highest severity rating that day, as an ordered factor.

The coding rules:

- **Event types.** "No" on a day the stress question was answered "No."
  Missing on a day the stress question itself is missing. Otherwise "Yes" if
  the box was checked and "No" if not.
- **Worst stressor.**
  - "None" if there was no stressful event.
  - Otherwise the highest severity rating, where the scale runs 1 = not at all
    to 4 = very.
  - Missing if the person said "Yes" but rated no event.
  - It is an ordered factor because the scale has only four options.

The group's cleaning (above) built these columns with the same rules. The
chunk below rebuilds both from the download with the rules above and
checks that every play day agrees.

```{r stress-check}
event_cols <- grep("^stress_events_", names(dat), value = TRUE)

# the gate question and the follow-ups agree: every "Yes" has a type checked
table(had_stress = dat$had_stress,
      any_type_yes = rowSums(sapply(dat[event_cols], function(x) x == "Yes")) > 0,
      useNA = "ifany")

# the rules above applied to the download, play days only
raw_play <- raw[match(paste(dat$id, dat$day), paste(raw$id, raw$day)), ]
rule_types <- sapply(event_cols, function(v)
  ifelse(is.na(raw_play$had_stress), NA, ifelse(!is.na(raw_play[[v]]), "Yes", "No")))
sev   <- as.matrix(raw_play[grep("^how_stressful_", names(raw_play))])
worst <- suppressWarnings(apply(sev, 1, max, na.rm = TRUE))
rule_worst <- ifelse(raw_play$had_stress == "No", 0,
                   ifelse(raw_play$had_stress == "Yes" & rowSums(!is.na(sev)) > 0,
                          worst, NA))

# same answers on every play day
stopifnot(identical(unname(rule_types), unname(sapply(dat[event_cols], as.character))))
stopifnot(identical(as.numeric(rule_worst),
                    as.numeric(as.integer(dat$stress_worst) - 1)))   # "No event" = 0

table(rules_above = rule_worst, group_cleaning = dat$stress_worst, useNA = "ifany")
```

The two codings agree on every play day. Two notes on the check:

- **The rule for a "Yes" with no type checked.** The group's cleaning makes
  the event types missing on such a day, while the rules above code them
  "No." The
  first table above shows that no play day has this pattern, so the two
  rules give the same data here.
- **The health/other swap.** The swap that the cleaning fixes does not
  change either column used here. The worst rating is the highest across all
  seven severity columns, whichever column a rating sits in. The event types
  come from the checkboxes, not the severity columns.

**Merging "Not at all" into "Not very."** The worst-stressor factor has four
levels: None < Not very < Somewhat < Very. Only
`r sum(dat$stress_worst == "Not at all", na.rm = TRUE)` play days have "Not
at all" as their worst rating. We code those days as "Not very" for three
reasons:

1. **Two days cannot support a level of their own.** The elastic net would
   estimate a contrast from two days, which is noise. With ten grouped
   folds, the level would be missing entirely from most folds' training or
   held-out data. The forest's smallest leaf is five days, so it could never
   isolate them.
2. **"Not very" is the nearest level.** Both mean the event was mild, and the
   two are neighbors on the ordered scale. Merging neighbors keeps the order
   that makes the variable ordinal.
3. **"None" would be wrong.** The person did report a stressful event, and
   that day's event types say so. Coding the worst rating "None" would
   contradict those columns on the same day.

The cost is negligible: two days out of
`r format(nrow(dat), big.mark = ",")`.

```{r stress-recode}
# shorter names for the event types
dat <- dat %>%
  rename(stress_argument       = stress_events_argument,
         stress_discrimination = stress_events_discrimination,
         stress_friend_family  = stress_events_friend_rel,
         stress_health         = stress_events_health,
         stress_home           = stress_events_home,
         stress_other          = stress_events_other,
         stress_work_school    = stress_events_work_school)

stress_types <- c("stress_argument", "stress_discrimination",
                  "stress_friend_family", "stress_health", "stress_home",
                  "stress_work_school", "stress_other")

# four levels; the duplicated label merges "Not at all" into "Not very"
dat$stress_worst <- factor(as.character(dat$stress_worst),
                           levels = c("No event", "Not at all", "Not very",
                                      "Somewhat", "Very"),
                           labels = c("None", "Not very", "Not very",
                                      "Somewhat", "Very"),
                           ordered = TRUE)

table(dat$stress_worst, useNA = "always")

# share of play days with each kind of event
sapply(dat[stress_types], function(x) round(100 * mean(x == "Yes", na.rm = TRUE), 1))
```

## Person characteristics from the intake survey

The intake survey came before the diary. The demographics are coded as
follows:

- **Age** is in years.
- **Gender** is man, woman, or non-binary / gender diverse. Typed answers are
  coded by the identity they state.
- **Employment** is full-time, part-time or self-employed, student, or not
  employed.
- **Education** is the highest level completed, numeric 1 to 6 (six ordered
  levels).
- **Relationship status** is single, partnered, or divorced / separated /
  widowed.
- **Cares for children** is yes if that caregiving box was checked, and no if
  the person answered the question without checking it.

"Prefer not to say" is a non-answer and becomes missing (Section 4).

```{r intake}
blank_na <- function(x) { x <- trimws(x); x[x == ""] <- NA; x }

emp <- tolower(blank_na(intake$employment))
ms  <- tolower(blank_na(intake$marital_status))
edu <- blank_na(intake$edu_level)

care_cols <- c("care_children", "care_elderly", "care_disability",
               "care_none", "care_other")
answered_care <- rowSums(!is.na(intake[care_cols]) & intake[care_cols] != "") > 0

person <- data.frame(
  id  = intake$pid,
  age = intake$age,
  gender = case_when(
    intake$gender %in% c("Man", "Transgender Man", "Transgender Man (FTM)") ~ "Man",
    intake$gender %in% c("Woman", "trans woman") ~ "Woman",
    intake$gender == "Prefer not to say" | is.na(blank_na(intake$gender)) ~ NA_character_,
    TRUE ~ "Non-binary / gender diverse"),
  employment = case_when(
    is.na(emp) | grepl("prefer not", emp)              ~ NA_character_,
    grepl("student", emp)                               ~ "Student",
    emp %in% c("working full-time", "military")         ~ "Full-time",
    emp == "working part-time" |
      grepl("self|freelanc|gig|streamer|prolific", emp) ~ "Part-time / self-employed",
    TRUE                                                ~ "Not employed"),
  education = case_when(
    edu %in% c("Less than a high school diploma or equivalent",
               "Completed Primary School")                    ~ 1,
    edu %in% c("High school graduate or equivalent",
               "Completed Secondary School")                  ~ 2,
    edu %in% c("Some college but no degree",
               "Some University but no degree",
               "Vocational or Similar")                       ~ 3,
    edu == "Associate degree"                                 ~ 4,
    edu %in% c("Bachelor's degree", "University Bachelors Degree") ~ 5,
    edu %in% c("Master's degree, professional degree, or doctoral degree",
               "Graduate or professional degree (MA, MS, MBA, PhD, etc)") ~ 6,
    TRUE                                                      ~ NA_real_),
  relationship = case_when(
    is.na(ms) | ms == "prefer not to say"                     ~ NA_character_,
    ms == "single, never married"                             ~ "Single",
    grepl("divorc|widow|^separated", ms)                      ~ "Divorced / separated / widowed",
    grepl("married|partner|engaged|relationship|living with|civil union", ms) ~ "Partnered",
    TRUE                                                      ~ NA_character_),
  cares_for_children = case_when(
    !is.na(intake$care_children) & intake$care_children != "" ~ "Yes",
    answered_care                                             ~ "No",
    TRUE                                                      ~ NA_character_),
  intake_date = intake$date,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  filter(id %in% dat$id)

# one intake record per person, so the join cannot duplicate days
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(person$id))

# every typed answer and where it went, for the people in the daily table
in_dat <- intake$pid %in% dat$id
table(intake$employment[in_dat], person$employment[match(intake$pid[in_dat], person$id)],
      useNA = "ifany")
table(intake$marital_status[in_dat], person$relationship[match(intake$pid[in_dat], person$id)],
      useNA = "ifany")
```

```{r intake-join}
n_before <- nrow(dat)

dat <- dat %>%
  left_join(person, by = "id") %>%
  mutate(gender       = factor(gender, levels = c("Man", "Woman",
                                                  "Non-binary / gender diverse")),
         employment   = factor(employment, levels = c("Full-time",
                                                      "Part-time / self-employed",
                                                      "Student", "Not employed")),
         relationship = factor(relationship, levels = c("Single", "Partnered",
                                                        "Divorced / separated / widowed")),
         cares_for_children = factor(cares_for_children, levels = c("No", "Yes")))

stopifnot(nrow(dat) == n_before)

# people in the daily table with no intake record
c(people_without_intake = sum(!unique(dat$id) %in% intake$pid))
```

## The daily table

```{r select-vars}
day_preds <- c("game_type", "play_context", "platform", "sleep_quality",
               "day_type", "had_stress", stress_types, "stress_worst")
person_preds <- c("age", "gender", "employment", "education", "relationship",
                  "cares_for_children")

days <- dat[c("id", "day", "date", "intake_date", "life_satisfaction",
              bangs, needs, day_preds, person_preds)]

dim(days)
str(days)
```

`id`, `day`, `date`, and `intake_date` are kept only to split by person and
to check leakage. They are removed before any model sees the data.

# 4. Missing Data

```{r vis-miss, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Missing values in the daily table. Black cells are missing."}
model_vars <- c("life_satisfaction", bangs, needs, day_preds, person_preds)

vis_miss(days[model_vars], warn_large_data = FALSE) +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 25, r = 60), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))
```

```{r gg-miss-var, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Percent missing for the target and each predictor."}
gg_miss_var(days[model_vars], show_pct = TRUE)
```

```{r pct-missing}
miss_table <- data.frame(
  variable    = model_vars,
  n_missing   = colSums(is.na(days[model_vars])),
  pct_missing = round(100 * colMeans(is.na(days[model_vars])), 2),
  row.names   = NULL)
miss_table[order(-miss_table$pct_missing), ]
```

## Why are they missing?

**Platform** is the only daily variable with substantial missingness. It is
missing almost entirely in the first months of the study, which suggests the question was added to the survey partway through:

```{r platform-by-month}
days %>%
  mutate(month = format(date, "%Y-%m")) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(days = n(),
            pct_platform_missing = round(100 * mean(is.na(platform)), 1),
            mean_life_sat = round(mean(life_satisfaction, na.rm = TRUE), 1))
```

```{r platform-target}
platform_target <- days %>%
  group_by(platform_missing = is.na(platform)) %>%
  summarise(days = n(),
            mean_life_sat = round(mean(life_satisfaction, na.rm = TRUE), 1))
platform_target
```

Missing platform depends on **when** someone took part, which is an observed
fact, and not on their life satisfaction. Mean life satisfaction is
`r platform_target$mean_life_sat[platform_target$platform_missing]` on days
with platform missing and
`r platform_target$mean_life_sat[!platform_target$platform_missing]` on days
with it recorded, so the gap does not mark a different kind of day. So it is
most likely **MAR**, and KNN imputation inside the recipe fits that
mechanism.

```{r platform-person}
# missing platform days, by whether the person gave a platform on other days
platform_gap <- days %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  mutate(answered_other_days = any(!is.na(platform))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(is.na(platform)) %>%
  count(answered_other_days)
platform_gap

# share of each person's answered days on their usual platform
# (people with 5 or more answered days)
usual_platform <- days %>%
  filter(!is.na(platform)) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  filter(n() >= 5) %>%
  summarise(share = max(table(platform)) / n())
round(mean(usual_platform$share), 2)
```

**A limitation.** KNN fills each missing platform from similar days of
other people. It does not look at the person's own answers on other days.
`r platform_gap$n[platform_gap$answered_other_days]` of the
`r sum(platform_gap$n)` missing days belong to people who gave a platform on
other days, and people played on their usual platform on
`r round(100 * mean(usual_platform$share))`% of their days. For those days,
the person's usual platform would likely be a better guess. We keep KNN, so
that platform is imputed like every other predictor.

**The intake variables** are missing for two reasons:

- **The person has no intake record.** The most likely cause is a gap in
  linking the two surveys, which would be close to MCAR.
- **The person chose "Prefer not to say."** This could be **MNAR**, because
  someone may decline a question because of their answer.

```{r intake-missing}
# people in the daily table, by why each intake answer is missing
said_prefer_not <- function(answers) grepl("prefer not", tolower(answers))
in_person <- match(person$id, intake$pid)
care_prefer_not <- !is.na(intake$care_prefer_not_say[in_person]) &
                   intake$care_prefer_not_say[in_person] != ""

intake_missing <- data.frame(
  variable         = person_preds,
  no_intake_record = n_distinct(days$id[!days$id %in% intake$pid]),
  declined         = c(age          = 0,
                       gender       = sum(said_prefer_not(intake$gender[in_person])),
                       employment   = sum(said_prefer_not(intake$employment[in_person])),
                       education    = sum(said_prefer_not(intake$edu_level[in_person])),
                       relationship = sum(said_prefer_not(intake$marital_status[in_person])),
                       cares_for_children = sum(is.na(person$cares_for_children) & care_prefer_not)),
  row.names = NULL)
# an intake record, no answer, and no "Prefer not to say": the question was skipped
intake_missing$skipped <- colSums(is.na(person[person_preds])) - intake_missing$declined
stopifnot(intake_missing$skipped >= 0)
intake_missing
```

Most missing intake values come from the
`r intake_missing$no_intake_record[1]` people with no intake record. Only
`r with(intake_missing[-1, ], min(declined + skipped))` to
`r with(intake_missing, max(declined + skipped))` people declined or skipped
any one question, so the part that could be MNAR is small.

So the categorical intake variables get their own "Not reported" level
instead of being imputed. Age and education are filled with the training
median inside the recipe. Both are person-level facts, so every day of a
person gets the same value, which KNN would not guarantee. For the people
with no intake record, the "Not reported" levels already mark them as
missing, so the median does not hide that. Only the
`r intake_missing$declined[intake_missing$variable == "education"]` people who
declined the education question are filled without such a marker.

```{r daily-missing}
daily_vars <- c(bangs, needs, "sleep_quality", "day_type", "play_context",
                "had_stress", stress_types, "stress_worst")
max_daily_missing <- max(miss_table$n_missing[miss_table$variable %in% daily_vars])

# each block is missing all at once: 0 or 6 items on every day
table(bangs_missing = rowSums(is.na(days[bangs])))
table(needs_missing = rowSums(is.na(days[needs])))
```

**The daily items** (the BANGS items, the needs items, sleep, stress, type of
day, play context) are each missing on `r max_daily_missing` play days or
fewer (`r round(100 * max_daily_missing / nrow(days), 1)`%). A day missing
one BANGS item is missing all six, and the same holds for the needs items.
These are unfinished surveys. Leaving a survey unfinished is unlikely to
depend on the answers never given, so these are close to **MCAR**. They are
imputed with KNN inside the recipe. KNN fills each column on its own, so on
an imputed day the stress columns may not agree with each other (for
example, `had_stress` "No" with an event type "Yes"). This can happen on at
most `r miss_table$n_missing[miss_table$variable == "had_stress"]` days.

**The worst stressor** would also be missing on a day the person said "Yes"
but rated no event.
`r sum(days$had_stress == "Yes" & is.na(days$stress_worst), na.rm = TRUE)`
play days have that pattern, so it is missing only when the stress question
itself is missing.

## Decisions

```{r drop-target}
c(missing_target = sum(is.na(days$life_satisfaction)))

days <- days %>% filter(!is.na(life_satisfaction))

counts <- rbind(counts, data.frame(step = "Play days with a target",
                                   days = nrow(days), people = n_distinct(days$id)))
counts

# days complete on every predictor, counted before the "Not reported" levels
# are added (afterwards those days would look complete)
c(complete_days = sum(complete.cases(days[model_vars])))

not_reported <- function(x) {
  factor(ifelse(is.na(x), "Not reported", as.character(x)),
         levels = c(levels(x), "Not reported"))
}
for (v in c("gender", "employment", "relationship", "cares_for_children")) {
  days[[v]] <- not_reported(days[[v]])
}

sapply(days[c("gender", "employment", "relationship", "cares_for_children")], table)
```

**Summary: how each kind of missing value is handled.**

| What is missing | Variables | Handling | Where and when | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Question skipped by design | social boxes on non-play days; stress types and severity when `had_stress` is No | Recoded to "No" / "No event", not imputed | Cleaning (Section 3) | The answer is known from the skip pattern |
| The play question | `played24hr` | Day dropped | Section 3 | Cannot tell whether it is a play day; nearly all are empty surveys |
| Every gaming answer on a play day | title, social boxes, platform, and all BANGS items | Day dropped | Section 3 | The day says nothing about the session |
| The target | `life_satisfaction` | Day dropped | Section 4, before the split | Nothing to train on or score |
| An unreadable or conflicting game title | `game_type` | "Unknown" level | Section 3 | A real category of answer, not a gap |
| A categorical intake answer | gender, employment, relationship, cares for children | "Not reported" level | Section 4, before the split | Declining may depend on the answer (MNAR); the level keeps that information |
| A numeric intake answer | age, education | Training median | Model recipes (Section 8), relearned in each fold | A fact about the person, so every day of a person gets the same value |
| A daily answer, in the models | BANGS items, needs items (set A), sleep, type of day, platform, `had_stress`, stress types, `stress_worst` | KNN, 5 neighbors, from the other predictors (never the target) | Model recipes (Section 8), relearned in each fold | Unfinished surveys (MCAR) and the late-added platform question (MAR) |
| A BANGS or needs block, before clustering and PCA | the 6 BANGS items, the 6 needs items | Training median | Block recipes (Section 6), learned once on the training days | The blocks must be filled first, and a day missing one item misses all six, so KNN has nothing to match on |
| Cluster and component scores | `play_day_type`, `need_satisfaction`, `need_frustration` | Nothing missing | Section 6 | Built from the already-filled blocks |

**The life satisfaction slider.** The values 0, 50, and 100 are kept as real
answers:

```{r target-distribution, fig.height = 3.5, fig.cap = "Life satisfaction on play days."}
summary(days$life_satisfaction)

ggplot(days, aes(life_satisfaction)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2) +
  labs(x = "Life satisfaction today (0 to 100)", y = "Days")
```

## The variable table

```{r variable-table}
pm <- function(v) paste0(miss_table$pct_missing[miss_table$variable == v], "%")
bangs_stem <- "\"In my most recent session of [game]...\" "
needs_stem <- "\"Today...\" "
agree7 <- " (1 to 7, strongly disagree to strongly agree)"
stress_stem <- "\"What kind of stressful event(s) occurred?\" Checkbox: "

var_table <- tibble::tribble(
  ~variable, ~source, ~item, ~treatment, ~daily_summary, ~missing,
  "life_satisfaction (target)", "daily", "\"I was satisfied with my life today.\" 0 to 100 slider", "Continuous target", "as rated (same day)", paste0(pm("life_satisfaction"), "; rows dropped"),
  "gaming_autonomy", "daily, play days", paste0(bangs_stem, "\"I could play in the way I wanted.\"", agree7), "Numeric; clustering block", "as rated, most recent session", paste0(pm("gaming_autonomy"), "; KNN"),
```
